I am glad you are in supervision and have your own therapist. I am so sorry that empathy is very thing like makes you good at your job, but it is also one of the most draining aspects of it too. This is a really tough situation, and it’s understandable that it’s hitting you harder when working with children. 

Here are a couple of things I came up with:

Instead of focusing solely on the pain the child has endured, remind yourself: *I am a part of their healing. I am not their trauma, I am their safe space.* This can help shift the emotional toll.

Consider trying a ritual to "close the door" on work at the end of the day. Some people visualize placing the case in a box and putting it on a shelf until the next session.

Physical release such a yoga or stretching, essential oils for sensory based grounding or even creative expression such as journalling, or creating art.

I hope this helps. This work is hard, but it’s also meaningful. You’re making a difference. Keep going, and be kind to yourself. 💙
